full_judgment:
4. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement stating inter alia that the suit is barred by limitation. It is further stated that the defendant’s vessel M.V. Rita was not in any way responsible or liable for the damage caused to the plaintiff's vessel R.F Kandra. It is their case that the plaintiff's case is absolutely misconceived and unfounded in view of the fact that the defendant's vessel had no occasion to touch Chandpur Ghat inasmuch as this is a direct launch from Dhaka to Barishal and it had no permission to take passengers from Chandpur Ghat for the aforesaid vessel M.V. Rita. In a word, the defendant denied the total liability in respect of the alleged claim of the plaintiff. 

 8. Let me take up issues Nos. 3, 4 and 5 together. It is the plain case of the plaintiff that the defendant's vessel M.V. Rita dashed the plaintiff's vessel R.F. Kandra at 2.00 P.M. on 26.9.85 at Chandpur Ghat and thereby caused the aforesaid damage and for such damage the plaintiff prayed for a decree before the Court. But the learned Advocate for the defendant has referred to the document namely, time table issued by IWTA on 13.7.85 which was valid up to 31.10.85. This time table is not disputed in any manner. From this time table, it appears that Masud Navigation Co. will play its vessel M.V. Rita from Dhaka to Barisal and Barisal to Dhaka directly and there was no stoppage to M.V. Rita at Chandpur Ghat in between the period from 13.7.85 to 31.10.85. Admittedly the collision took place on 26.9.85. Relying on this document the learned Advocate for the defendant submits that there had been not occasion for the vessel of the defendant to cause any damage to the vessel of the plaintiff on 26.9.85 at 2-00 P.M. at Chandpur Ghat. He further submits that this fact is further supported by the fact that the plaintiff made out a case that M.V. Rita caused damage to R.F. Kandra but there was no damage on the body of the Rita. Had there been any collision between the two vessels, naturally it would cause damage to both the vessels and the defendant’s vessel would get at least some sign of damage as a result of collision. The plaintiff failed to produce any cogent evidence to show that in fact the defendant’s vessel had a permission to touch Chandpur Ghat and it actually touched the Chandpur Ghat on 26.9.85 and in course of touching or coming out from Chandpur Ghat it caused damage to this vessel R.F. Kandra. In view of the above, it appears to me that plaintiff has totally failed to make out a case that defendant's vessel M.V. Rita had caused damage to the plaintiff's vessel R.F. Kandra on 26.9.85 at 2-00 P.M. at Chandpur Ghat.
